header: Date: 2026-03-09 | Start: 10:30 AM PST | Duration: ~55m | Recording: yes | Location: Zoom | Attendees: Ethan Park (Redwood AE), Priya Malhotra (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (NeuraTech Head of ML), Omar Reyes (NeuraTech Platform), Sonia Patel (NeuraTech Security)
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on capacity readout from the pilot, tuning notes, and planning burst/autoscale behavior for Dedicated pool. Team agreed on an additional 30-minute sustained load test, clarified burst pricing mechanics, and outlined VPC/security checklist. Remaining open: customer to provide detailed request size distribution and cache hit metrics; Redwood to produce formal burst addendum and updated cost projection.
topics: Autoscaling policy and burst capacity design
Dedicated pool sizing and pre-warm strategy
transcript: 00:00 - Ethan: Alright everyone, thanks for joining — let's kick off. Quick roll call?
00:08 - Maya: Maya here, hi. Omar and Sonia on my side as well.
00:12 - Omar: Omar, hello.
00:15 - Sonia: Sonia, security. Good morning.
00:20 - Priya: Priya from Redwood, we'll pick up where we left off on the capacity numbers.

01:02 - Ethan: Topline from last week's pilot: average p95 latency across the test routes was 220 to 280 ms depending on prompt length; tail spikes to about 420 ms during the 95-99th. We're seeing KV cache helping most short requests — Omar do those numbers line up with what you captured?

01:25 - Omar: Yeah similar, although our logs show a slightly higher tail when we include retries. There's a cluster of long requests from the anonymized search endpoint that skewed the 99s. Also our mean token length jumped during the Friday batch run — might be workload noise.

02:10 - Priya: On the Redwood side we broke out throughput by model variant; the 13B quantized flavor holds up well for medium prompts, but for heavier prompts we saw GPU saturation — that's where the burst plan needs to help. We've attached the charts in the drive link (see shared deck).
02:45 - Maya: Can you remind us how Redwood handles burst vs reserved capacity? The distinction in the docs was a bit fuzzy for us.

03:00 - Ethan: Sure. Dedicated gives you a reserved pool for baseline. Burst is an overlay that can spin up additional capacity for short windows; pricing for burst is higher per-hour and it can be throttled by account limits. Important: bursts can be pre-warmed or lazy — pre-warm reduces cold starts at cost of reservation time.
03:18 - Sonia: From a compliance side we need to know what data touching the burst instances looks like — same VPC? Are logs forwarded? KMS keys?

03:30 - Priya: Good question. In Private/Dedicated deployments we keep data in the customer's VPC; for hosted Dedicated with burst we still use customer VPC peering, traffic stays within the peered network, and KMS integration remains the same. Logs can be forwarded or kept in Redwoods audit bucket per policy. I'll follow up with the SOC2 artifact — sorry, the SOC2 doc — to show exactly what fields are logged.
04:05 - Omar: How long is a burst spin-up typically? We saw some 60–90s cold times during Friday's ramp.

04:16 - Priya: Cold spin-up can vary: 30–120s depending on model and quantization warm paths. Pre-warm reduces that to under 20s but costs reserved buffer. We can suggest a hybrid: keep 1–2 warm instances for critical low-latency routes and allow 2–4 burst nodes to scale based on queue depth. That fits your SLOs?
04:45 - Maya: Our SLO is 95% under 300ms for interactive UI calls, but batch jobs can tolerate more. We want the UI to never hit degraded mode during predictable campaigns.

05:02 - Ethan: Right. For that SLO we'd recommend baseline pool sized to cover steady-state plus expected 95th of normal traffic, and burst cushion for the top 5–10% traffic spikes. Based on current pilot metrics, that suggests adding a burst allowance of ~30–40% of baseline for peak campaigns.
05:30 - Omar: Can you show the math? We need concrete VM/GPU counts — our infra team needs exact numbers for capacity planning.

05:45 - Priya: Sure — quick calc from last week's 10k RPS equivalent: baseline needed for steady 8k RPS at median token length is 4x A100-40GB sized workers (we measured roughly 2.1 concurrent requests per GPU for medium prompts). Peak Saturdays jumped to 12k RPS — so burst of 2x more workers. I'll export the sizing table after the call.
06:25 - Maya: The 2.1 requests per GPU sounds low — are you factoring batching? We do a lot of small requests so batching might be low, but can we tune batching windows?

06:35 - Priya: Yes, batching is configurable. We saw your traffic has a high fraction of short 1–2 token responses which gives less batching efficiency. We can increase max batch latency to 10–12ms for those routes — that yields better utilization but slightly increases median latency. It's a tradeoff.
07:02 - Omar: Will adjusting batching affect token-level costs?

07:08 - Ethan: Slightly — higher batching lowers per-token compute cost so total spend can drop, but if you increase latency beyond UI thresholds it's not good. We'll run a cost vs latency sensitivity and share the curve.
08:00 - Maya: Regarding the 99th percentile spikes, are those mostly queueing or kernel-level stalls?

08:10 - Priya: Mostly queueing during sudden ramps and occasional kernel contention when sequence lengths spike. We instrumented with Redwood Console traces — a couple of requests hit a slow path in ops fusion for long sequences. We recommended a model quantization tweak and a per-route max tokens ceiling to bound worst-case.
09:00 - Sonia: For security sign-off, we need a clear statement that burst instances honor the same KMS/HSM keys and that logs are auditable. Also, can we restrict burst to approved regions?
09:18 - Ethan: Yes, bursts are regional and can be constrained. KMS keys are the same; burst nodes join the same VPC peering and use your KMS. We'll provide the network diagram and the KMS flow doc.
10:10 - Omar: One practical ask — can Redwood expose a soft-limit alarm when queued requests exceed X for more than Y seconds so we can trigger fallback to a lite-model?

10:24 - Priya: Absolutely. We have route-level thresholds and can configure a fallback policy: when queue depth > threshold we route to a smaller model or to cached responses. We can demo that in the next run.

11:02 - Maya: Pricing: we got the initial estimate but need the burst addendum — hourly delta and monthly cap. Can you produce a 30-day cost projection for March-level traffic + a 2-day campaign spike?
11:20 - Ethan: We'll do that. We'll include run-rate and worst-case burst APUs. Expect the spreadsheet in 48 hours.
12:05 - Omar: For the load test you proposed next Tuesday, what inputs do you need from us? Sequence length distribution? Auth tokens?
12:18 - Priya: We need the request size histogram, typical prompt templates to simulate real CPU work, and a test API key we've scoped to a dev project. No prod credentials needed.
12:45 - Maya: We'll get that over. Also, can you codify the autoscale policy in a playbook? We'd like to hand it to ops.

13:00 - Priya: Yes, we'll deliver a playbook with recommended thresholds, pre-warm counts, and escalation steps. We'll also include the block diagram for VPC peering, allowed IPs, and log retention levels.
14:02 - Sonia: One other point: audit logging retention — default 30 days is fine for now but for compliance we might want 90. Is that an add-on?
14:12 - Ethan: Extended retention is an add-on; we'll quote it.
15:00 - Omar: Any concerns about model fallbacks changing output quality during spikes? We need guardrails to avoid user-visible regressions.

15:10 - Priya: We'll tie fallbacks to a predefined smaller model that your team validated with the same prompt set — we'll run A/B quality checks during the load test to measure regression. Redwood Optimize can alert if quality delta exceeds threshold.
16:00 - Maya: Sounds good. Can we capture the main decisions before we close?

16:10 - Ethan: Decision 1: run 30m sustained 90% RPS test with the proposed load profile next Tuesday. Decision 2: Redwood will produce burst pricing addendum and 30-day + campaign cost projections. Decision 3: Put 1–2 pre-warmed warm instances per critical route and allow up to 40% burst cushion during campaigns. Decision 4: Redwood to supply SOC2 summary and VPC peering diagram.
16:50 - Omar: I'll get the histograms and test key to Priya by Monday.
17:05 - Priya: Great — I'll also drop the load test script and schedule a 30-minute window in your calendar. Ethan will send pricing.
17:30 - Sonia: Thanks all, please include the KMS flow and confirmation that logs during burst show the same audit fields.
17:50 - Ethan: Will do. Anything else?
18:05 - Maya: No, that's it. Thanks everyone.
18:10 - Ethan: Thanks — we'll follow up on the action items. End call.
